title: "Stokastisk – Python SDK for vLLM Inference on Kaggle Dual NVIDIA T4 GPUs"
pagetitle: "Stokastisk – Python SDK for vLLM Inference on Kaggle Dual NVIDIA T4 GPUs"
description-meta: "Stokastisk is an independent open-source Python 3.13 SDK for Kaggle's dual NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPUs: bundled vLLM 0.25.1, Triton attention (SM75), structured output, an OpenAI-compatible server and tensor, pipeline and replica parallelism."
---

**Stokastisk is an independent open-source Python SDK that runs a bundled vLLM 0.25.1 inference engine on Kaggle's dual NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPUs (SM75, CUDA 13.0) with Triton attention (`TRITON_ATTN`), installed with one `pip` command.**

It is not affiliated with vLLM, NVIDIA, Kaggle or any company named Stochastic. See the [FAQ](user-guide/faq.html).

## Install

In a Kaggle notebook with *GPU T4 × 2*, *Internet ON* and Python 3.13, pin the wheel by URL and SHA256 with PyPI as the only index:

```bash
!python -m pip install --index-url https://pypi.org/simple "stokastisk @ https://huggingface.co/waqasm86/stokastisk/resolve/main/wheels/stokastisk-0.1.0-5-cp313-cp313-linux_x86_64.whl#sha256=fe80d7c36fa78cf8a26feb1e00bb5f1f006ca45a027450353603976320ae0b3e"
```

More options and verification: [Install Stokastisk on Kaggle](user-guide/installation.html).

## First generation

```python
from stokastisk import LLM, StokastiskConfig

with LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", config=StokastiskConfig(max_model_len=2048)) as llm:
    print(llm.verify_attention_backend())                 # TRITON_ATTN
    print(llm.complete("The capital of France is", max_tokens=16))
```

## What it provides

| Capability | Where to read |
|---|---|
| Validated configuration and T4 defaults | [Configuration](user-guide/configuration.html) |
| `LLM`: generate, chat, complete, safe close | [The LLM engine](user-guide/engine.html) |
| JSON-schema output with pinned xgrammar | [Structured output](user-guide/structured-output.html) |
| OpenAI-compatible server, streaming, metrics | [OpenAI-compatible server](user-guide/openai-server.html) |
| TP=2, experimental PP=2, independent replicas | [Parallelism](user-guide/parallelism.html) |
| Topology, memory estimates, CUDA, NCCL | [Topology](user-guide/topology-and-memory.html), [CUDA and NCCL](user-guide/cuda-nccl-communication.html) |
| Telemetry and benchmarks | [Telemetry and benchmarking](user-guide/telemetry-benchmarking.html) |
| Offline model and feature checks | [Diagnostics](user-guide/diagnostics-compatibility.html) |
| Every public class and function | [API reference](reference/index.html) |

## What has actually been verified

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-0.5B (TP=1, TP=2, PP=2, replicas), Qwen2.5-3B (TP=2, PP=2) and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (TP=2, PP=2) ran on Kaggle 2 × T4 with `TRITON_ATTN` | **Kaggle-tested on wheel build 3** (now withdrawn) |
| The current wheel, **build 5**, was not itself run on Kaggle | it differs from build 3 only in compatibility reporting and one error message; build 3's evidence is **inherited**, and build 5 is **verified on CPU** |
| Other models, other GPUs, throughput | **not claimed** |

Read the full account in [Release verification](user-guide/release-verification.html), [Kaggle notebooks and evidence](user-guide/kaggle-examples.html) and [Production readiness and limitations](user-guide/production-limitations.html).
